title: GH#15234: fix issue-sync duplicate issues from silent gh create failure + limit 50
body:
## Summary

Fixes all four root causes of duplicate GitHub issues identified in #15234.

- **Fix 1** (`_push_create_issue`): Replace silent `2>/dev/null` with stderr capture. On non-zero exit or empty URL, attempt a recovery lookup via `gh_find_issue_by_title` before declaring failure. Handles the case where `gh issue create` creates the issue server-side but returns empty stdout (e.g. when label application fails after creation).
- **Fix 2** (`gh_find_issue_by_title`): Increase default `--limit` from `50` to `500`. With `--limit 50`, issues created >50 issues ago are invisible to dedup checks in repos with 500+ issues.
- **Fix 3** (all call sites): Update all 5 explicit `limit=50` call sites to `500` (race-condition guard, `_push_process_task`, `cmd_enrich`, `cmd_close`, `cmd_reconcile`).
- **Fix 4** (`issue-sync.yml`): Change `cancel-in-progress` from `true` to `false` in `sync-on-push` job. A cancelled run after issue creation but before ref write-back produces the same orphaned-issue pattern as Fix 1.
- **Fix 5** (`cmd_pull`): Check file modification via `md5sum` before printing `Added ref:GH#...` success message. Previously printed success even when `add_gh_ref_to_todo` silently skipped (ref already existed), making debugging harder.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` — Fixes 1–5
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` — Fix 4

Closes #15234

title: fix: screen-time tracking fallback for macOS 26.3+ (isBacklit deprecated)
body:
## Summary

- macOS 26.3.1 deprecated the `/display/isBacklit` Knowledge DB stream (stopped recording March 22, 2026), breaking all screen time tracking for the GitHub profile README and health dashboards.
- Adds `/app/usage` as an automatic fallback: detects stale isBacklit data (>3 days since last event) and switches to per-app usage aggregate.
- Also updates `_macos_earliest_date()` to check both streams for snapshot coverage.

## Impact

- Profile README "Screen time" row was showing stale/incorrect numbers since March 22
- Screen-time JSONL snapshots were missing 11 days of data (now backfilled)
- The `/display/isBacklit` deprecation also caused the `screen-time-snapshot` launchd job to output "No screen time data available" silently

## Testing

- ShellCheck: clean
- Boundary tests: 5/5 pass
- Manual verification: `query 1` → 11.2h, `query 7` → 83.5h, `query 28` → 239.0h (was 0h/0h/228.7h before fix)
- `snapshot` successfully backfilled 11 missing days from `/app/usage`

title: fix: worker sessions not persisted to shared DB (auth isolation side effect)
body:
## Summary

- Worker sessions since April 1 have been invisible to session-time stats because `XDG_DATA_HOME` redirection for auth isolation inadvertently moved the entire OpenCode data directory to a per-worker temp dir
- Each worker created a disposable `opencode.db` in `/tmp/aidevops-worker-auth.XXXXXX/opencode/` that was discarded on exit
- This caused "AI worker hours" to show 0.0h for 24h on the profile README despite active worker dispatches

## Root Cause

`headless-runtime-helper.sh:1263` sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` to isolate OAuth `auth.json` per worker. OpenCode uses `XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/opencode.db` for session persistence, so the isolation also redirected the session DB.

## Fix

Set `OPENCODE_DB` (supported by OpenCode) to point to the shared DB before redirecting `XDG_DATA_HOME`. Auth stays isolated, sessions go to the shared DB. `OPENCODE_DB` is already in the `OPENCODE_*` sandbox passthrough pattern.

## Impact

- ~2 days of worker session data lost (April 1-3) -- sessions ran successfully but weren't recorded
- Worker hours will resume tracking immediately after merge + deploy
- No data recovery needed; the headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl has the activity data as a secondary source

Completes the PIM tool suite. - **macOS**: Apple Notes via `osascript` (no install needed, iCloud sync automatic) - **Linux/Windows**: `nb` CLI notebook (Markdown, git-backed sync) - **Commands**: `setup`, `folders`, `show`, `add`, `view`, `search`, `delete`, `sync` Closes #16096 ## Changes | File | Change | |---|---| | `.agents/scripts/notes-helper.sh` | **NEW** — cross-platform notes CLI (658 lines) | | `.agents/tools/productivity/notes.md` | **NEW** — subagent doc with usage guide | | `.agents/scripts/setup/_tools.sh` | Added Notes to PIM tool setup (macOS: no-op, Linux: installs `nb`) | | `.agents/subagent-index.toon` | Registered `notes` in productivity subagents | | `.agents/tools/productivity/apple-reminders.md` | Added cross-reference to `notes.md` | | `.agents/tools/productivity/calendar.md` | Added cross-reference to `notes.md` | | `.agents/tools/productivity/contacts.md` | Added cross-reference to `notes.md` | ## Runtime Testing - **Risk level**: Low (new agent tool, docs, no runtime code paths) - **Verification**: `self-assessed` — ShellCheck clean (zero violations), `bash -n` syntax OK - No existing tests to break; additive-only changes to existing files ## Key Decisions 1. **`nb` over `joplin`**: `nb` is CLI-native, shell-based, Markdown files — fits the pattern of lightweight CLI tools (khal, khard, todoman). ## What

title: t1865: add TTL + process liveness check to dispatch-comment dedup guard
body:
## Summary

- Reduces `DISPATCH_COMMENT_MAX_AGE` from 4h to 1h — aligns with `STALE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` used by Layer 6
- Adds process liveness check after a 5-min grace period: if a dispatch comment is within the TTL but no worker process is running for that issue, the comment is treated as stale and re-dispatch is allowed
- Configurable via `DISPATCH_COMMENT_GRACE_SECONDS` env var (default 300s)

## Problem

Worker throughput was capped at ~10/24 slots because stale dispatch comments from dead workers blocked re-dispatch for up to 4 hours. The dedup guard (Layer 5) couldn't distinguish "worker in-flight" from "worker dead, comment left behind".

Evidence from this session: 7 open issues (#16529, #16516, #16515, #16496, #16480, #16414, #15262) were blocked solely by stale dispatch comments from workers that had completed 2-4h ago.

## Testing

**Before fix (original script):**
```
#16529: BLOCKED — dispatch comment by marcusquinn posted 8884s ago
#16516: BLOCKED — dispatch comment by marcusquinn posted 9951s ago
#16480: BLOCKED — dispatch comment by marcusquinn posted 12323s ago
```

**After fix (modified script):**
```
#16529: CLEAR — safe to dispatch
#16516: CLEAR — safe to dispatch
#16480: CLEAR — safe to dispatch
```

All 7 previously-blocked issues now clear. ShellCheck clean.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Medium** (dispatch infrastructure, no data loss risk). Assessment: `self-assessed` — tested with real production issues and confirmed correct behavior for both stale and active scenarios.

## Key decisions

- 1h TTL chosen to align with the existing stale assignment threshold (Layer 6), providing consistent behavior across dedup layers
- 5-min grace period avoids racing with worker startup (process may not be visible in `pgrep` immediately after dispatch)
- Process liveness check is same-machine only; cross-machine dedup is handled by Layer 6 (assignee guard with stale recovery)

Closes #16626

title: t1866: feat: autoagent — autonomous framework self-improvement agent and command
body:
<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->
## What

Implements the autoagent system for autonomous framework self-improvement — an agent that mines signals from operational data, generates improvement hypotheses across 6 types, applies modifications to framework files, evaluates with multi-trial measurement, and keeps only consistent improvements.

## Issue

Closes #16656

## Files Changed

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `.agents/scripts/autoagent-metric-helper.sh` | t1867: composite scorer (comprehension + lint + tokens) |
| `.agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent.md` | t1868: main autoagent subagent |
| `.agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent/signal-mining.md` | t1868: signal extraction from session logs, pulse outcomes, git |
| `.agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent/hypothesis-types.md` | t1868: 6 hypothesis types with progression strategy |
| `.agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent/safety.md` | t1868: never-modify, regression gate, security exemptions, overfitting |
| `.agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent/evaluation.md` | t1868: multi-trial pseudocode, trajectory recording |
| `.agents/scripts/commands/autoagent.md` | t1869: /autoagent command (4 invocation patterns) |
| `.agents/templates/autoagent-program-template.md` | t1871: program template with 3 examples |
| `.agents/tools/autoresearch/autoresearch/loop.md` | t1870: multi-trial evaluation extension |

## Testing

**Risk level:** Low — documentation and shell scripts only. No runtime state changes.

**Acceptance criteria verified:**

- [x] `/autoagent` command exists: `.agents/scripts/commands/autoagent.md`
- [x] Autoagent subagent + 4 subdocs: all 5 files present
- [x] `autoagent-metric-helper.sh` passes `shellcheck` (zero violations)
- [x] Research program template contains `hypothesis_types`, `signal_sources`, `safety`
- [x] Multi-trial evaluation documented in `autoresearch/loop.md` (pattern: `trials:`)
- [x] All shell scripts pass shellcheck
- [x] All markdown files pass markdownlint (0 errors across 8 files)

**Verification commands:**

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/autoagent-metric-helper.sh
markdownlint-cli2 ".agents/tools/autoagent/**/*.md" ".agents/scripts/commands/autoagent.md"
test -f .agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent.md && echo "PASS"
grep -qE "multi.trial|trials:" .agents/tools/autoresearch/autoresearch/loop.md && echo "PASS"
```

## Key Decisions

1. **Extends autoresearch, not a replacement** — same loop infrastructure (worktrees, results TSV, memory, mailbox, budget enforcement, crash recovery). Only edit surface, metric source, and hypothesis generator differ.
2. **Does NOT integrate Harbor directly** — domain mismatch (Harbor evaluates agents in Docker containers against standardized benchmarks; we modify a live framework). Adopted Harbor's design patterns (multi-trial sweeps, trajectory recording, overfitting prevention) without the dependency.
3. **Composite metric v1**: comprehension tests + linter checks — cheap, fast feedback. Token ratio as third component.
4. **6 hypothesis types** from kevinrgu/autoagent analysis: tool engineering and agent composition are high-leverage axes that pure prompt tuning misses.
5. **Overfitting test** adopted directly: "If this exact test disappeared, would this still be a worthwhile framework improvement?"
6. **Multi-trial default: 1** — backward compatible with all existing autoresearch programs.

## Runtime Testing

Self-assessed (Low risk). All deliverables are documentation and a shell script. The shell script has graceful degradation for all optional dependencies (`agent-test-helper.sh`, `shellcheck`, `markdownlint-cli2`).

title: t1870: multi-trial evaluation extension for autoresearch loop
body:
<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->
## What
Extends the autoresearch loop infrastructure to support multi-trial evaluation, reducing noise from stochastic metrics (e.g., LLM-scored tests). Changes 4 existing files.

## Issue
Closes #16660

## Files Changed
- `.agents/tools/autoresearch/autoresearch/loop.md` — added `multi_trial_evaluate` function, integrated into main loop, added consistency check
- `.agents/tools/autoresearch/autoresearch/logging.md` — added `trials` and `trial_variance` columns to TSV schema and examples
- `.agents/templates/research-program-template.md` — added `trials:` field to `## Budget` section with documentation
- `.agents/tools/autoresearch/autoresearch.md` — added `TRIALS` to Step 0 variable table, updated TSV header, fixed pre-existing MD038 lint error

## Key Changes

### loop.md
- `multi_trial_evaluate(metric_cmd, n_trials, per_experiment_timeout)` — runs metric N times, returns `(median, variance, trial_results)`. Any trial execution failure = overall ERROR (infrastructure problem, not noise).
- Main loop: when `TRIALS > 1`, calls `multi_trial_evaluate`; otherwise falls back to single-shot `run_metric()`.
- Consistency check: if median improves but `improvement_count <= TRIALS / 2`, logs `discard_inconsistent` and continues. Prevents false positives from lucky single trials.
- `log_result` calls updated to pass `TRIALS` and `variance` arguments.

### logging.md
- TSV format extended with `trials` (int) and `trial_variance` (float|`-`) columns.
- `status` column now includes `discard_inconsistent` as a valid value.
- Example rows updated to show both single-trial (`-` variance) and multi-trial rows.

### research-program-template.md
- `trials: 1` added to `## Budget` section with inline comment and explanatory paragraph.
- Default `1` preserves backward compatibility with all existing research programs.

### autoresearch.md
- `TRIALS` row added to Step 0 variable table (source: `## Budget` section, `trials:` line, default: 1).
- TSV header in Step 1.3 updated to include `pass_rate`, `token_ratio`, `trials`, `trial_variance` (was missing `pass_rate` and `token_ratio` too).

## Testing
- All 6 acceptance criteria verified via `grep -E` pattern matching against modified files.
- `markdownlint` passes clean on all 4 modified files (also fixed pre-existing MD038 error in autoresearch.md).
- Risk level: **Low** (documentation/pseudocode only — no executable code changed).

## Key Decisions
- **Median not mean**: robust to outliers; a single anomalous trial (e.g., LLM timeout → 0 score) doesn't drag down the result.
- **Fail on any trial error**: execution failure = infrastructure problem, not measurement noise. Fail fast.
- **Majority consistency check**: `improvement_count > TRIALS / 2` required. A 1-of-3 improvement is noise; 2-of-3 is signal.
- **Default trials:1**: zero behavior change for existing programs. Multi-trial is opt-in.

title: t1867: autoagent-metric-helper.sh — composite fitness scorer
body:
## Summary

- Implements `.agents/scripts/autoagent-metric-helper.sh` — the fitness function for the autoagent self-improvement loop
- 6 subcommands: `score`, `comprehension`, `lint`, `tokens`, `baseline`, `compare`
- Composite formula: `0.6 * comprehension + 0.3 * lint - 0.1 * max(0, token_ratio - 1.0)`, weights configurable via `--weights`

| Criterion | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Script exists and is executable | PASS |
| ShellCheck `--severity=warning` zero violations | PASS |
| `score` outputs single float matching `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` | PASS |

- Lint scoring uses changed files vs main (or capped 20-file sample) for performance — running shellcheck on all 430 scripts takes >60s due to source chain expansion (see `.shellcheckrc` GH#2915)

title: GH#16694: add token cost advisory to OpenCode plugin
body:
## Summary

- Add token cost advisory system to the aidevops OpenCode plugin that warns users when session context exceeds 200k tokens
- Fires at 200k, then every 50k above (250k, 300k, ...) via synthetic message injection in `messagesTransformHook`
- The LLM naturally relays the advisory to the user, suggesting `/compact` to reduce ongoing costs

Closes #16694

## Motivation

Sessions on large-context models (Gemini 1M+) or with autocompact disabled can accumulate hundreds of thousands of tokens. Each interaction becomes more expensive as context grows. Autocompact only fires near the model's context limit (e.g., ~980k for Gemini 1M), so users on those models get no cost feedback until it's too late.

## Implementation

All changes in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`:

- `getTokenTotal()` — computes token total matching OpenCode's `session-context-metrics.ts` calculation
- `checkTokenAdvisory()` — walks messages backwards to find the last assistant message with tokens, checks against threshold schedule (200k initial, 50k interval), per-session dedup via `tokenAdvisoryState` Map
- `buildTokenAdvisoryMessage()` — constructs synthetic user message instructing the LLM to inform the user about `/compact`
- Advisory check integrated into `messagesTransformHook` before existing TTSR violation checks

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk**: Low (agent prompt/plugin code, no runtime-critical paths)
- **Verification**: `self-assessed` — module load test + threshold logic test (3 scenarios: initial fire at 200k, suppression on repeat, re-fire at 250k bracket)

title: GH#14459: output UPDATE_AVAILABLE to stdout and add auto-update awareness
body:
## Summary

- **Fix**: `UPDATE_AVAILABLE` string was captured by `$()` command substitution into a variable but never echoed to stdout — AI agents running step 1 of the update check got empty output. Now echoed before early return.
- **Feature**: Detects whether the auto-update scheduler (launchd on macOS, cron on Linux) is active and appends `AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED` to the output, so the AI tells users "Auto-update is enabled and will apply this within ~10 minutes" instead of prompting manual update.
- Updated instruction text in all 3 locations: `templates/opencode-config-agents.md`, `generate-runtime-config.sh`, `generate-opencode-agents.sh`.

Closes #14459

title: t1872: add repos.json structural docs + write-time jq validation
body:
## Summary

- Documents `initialized_repos` array structure in AGENTS.md — entries MUST go inside the array, not as top-level keys
- Adds `jq empty` validation at all 5 repos.json write sites (detect-app-type.sh, profile-readme-helper.sh x3, pulse-wrapper.sh)
- Invalid JSON is caught before `mv` overwrites the live file, with error message and `rm` of the bad temp file

## Problem

A malformed repos.json entry (bare object without a key, outside the `initialized_repos` array) caused `jq` to fail silently in the pulse wrapper. The pulse saw zero repos in schedule window and stopped dispatching entirely — 17+ minute outage with zero workers despite 24 available slots.

Root cause: no validation existed at any write site. The AGENTS.md docs listed fields but never specified the array structure.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/AGENTS.md` | Added structural note to repo registration section |
| `.agents/scripts/detect-app-type.sh` | Added `jq empty` validation before `mv` |
| `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh` | Added `jq empty` validation at 3 write sites |
| `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` | Added `jq empty` validation before `mv` |

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Low** (docs + defensive validation guards, no behavior change on valid JSON). Assessment: `self-assessed` — ShellCheck clean, validation pattern is standard jq idiom.

Closes #16746

title: GH#16786: fix simplification scanner state mismatch and permission gate
body:
## Summary

- **State file migration**: 33 entries were stranded at the top level of `simplification-state.json` instead of under `.files`. The scanner only reads `.files`, so these already-simplified files were treated as "new" every pulse cycle, creating duplicate issues indefinitely.
- **Scanner resilience**: `check_file_state()` and `batch_hash_check()` now fall back to top-level lookup if `.files` misses, preventing recurrence.
- **Permission gate**: `run_weekly_complexity_scan()` now checks collaborator permission before creating issues. Non-collaborators (e.g. milohiss) were filing simplification issues on repos they don't have write access to.
- **Conditional `needs-maintainer-review`**: Label is now skipped when the authenticated user IS the repo maintainer — the standard auto-dispatch + PR review flow provides sufficient gating.

Closed 17 spurious issues created by non-collaborator instances.

Closes #16786

title: fix: worker launch failures from deploy race and tight validation timeout
body:
## Summary

- **Atomic deploy**: `setup.sh` now deploys to a staging directory then atomically swaps via `mv`, eliminating the window where scripts are missing mid-deploy. Previously clean+copy in-place caused `headless-runtime-helper.sh: No such file or directory` when the pulse dispatched workers during an update.
- **Launch timeout**: Raised `PULSE_LAUNCH_GRACE_SECONDS` from 20s to 35s. Sandbox-exec + opencode cold-start takes ~25-30s; the old 20s window caused false-positive launch failures for workers that started successfully.

Root cause analysis from worker logs:
- `/tmp/pulse-marcusquinn-aidevops-16797.log` (171 bytes): `No such file or directory` — deploy race
- `/tmp/pulse-marcusquinn-aidevops-16802.log` (306 bytes): output truncated mid-sentence — timeout too tight

title: t1874: detect reverse drift in issue-sync status and reconcile
body:
## Summary

- Add reverse drift detection to `issue-sync-helper.sh` `status` and `reconcile` commands
- Detects open TODO `[ ]` entries whose `ref:GH#` points to a closed GitHub issue
- Previously invisible — `status` reported "In sync" despite 75 of 87 open TODOs referencing closed issues

## Approach

Builds a set of open issue numbers from the already-fetched bulk `gh issue list` API response, then cross-references open TODO `ref:GH#` values against it. Zero additional API calls per task — the open issue list was already being fetched for forward drift detection.

## Before/After

**Before:**
```
=== Sync Status (marcusquinn/aidevops) ===
TODO open: 87 (87 ref, 0 no ref) | done: 1278
GitHub open: 23 closed: 500 | drift: 0
[SUCCESS] In sync
```

**After:**
```
[WARNING] REVERSE-DRIFT: t1741 ref:GH#15340 — TODO open but issue closed
... (75 items)

=== Sync Status (marcusquinn/aidevops) ===
TODO open: 87 (87 ref, 0 no ref) | done: 1278
GitHub open: 23 closed: 500 | drift: 0 | reverse-drift: 75
[WARNING] 75 open TODOs reference closed issues — run 'reconcile' to review
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` | Add reverse drift loop to `cmd_status()` and `cmd_reconcile()`, update summary output format, update help text |

Closes #16840
